newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill Pakistani Shi'ite leader, four others.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill Pakistani Shi'ite leader, four others.

text.p: Gunmen on motorcycles killed a Pakistani Shi'ite Moslem sect leader and four other people on Tuesday in an ambush of their car in the Punjab province capital of Lahore, police said.

They said Zulfikar Naqvi, provincial vice-president of the Shi'ite Tehrik-i-Jafaria party, his son Hamaad Naqvi, and their driver died instantly after the five unidentified gunmen fired bursts of Kalashnikov assault rifles at them.
A friend of the Shi'ite leader and a police guard accompanying them in the car died later at hospital, the police said.

They said they had no immediate information about the identity of the gunmen, who fled after the shooting, or the motive of the attack, which happened three days after unknown gunmen killed the provincial ombudsman in Lahore, retired Supreme Court judge Munir Ahmad Khan.

But Tehrik-i-Jafaria, representing the minority Shi'ite sect, and its rival Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan militant group from the majority Sunni sect have often accused each other of attacking their activists and mosques.
The official APP news agency quoted a senior police official as saying the police were yet to determine whether Tuesday's killings were the result of terrorism or a sectarian clash.
The incident follows a police report on Monday that they had arrested the chief of the Shi'ite militant group Sipah-i-Mohammad, Ghulam Raza Naqvi, and recovered 12 rocket-launchers from him.

Sunni-Shi'ite disputes over Islamic beliefs have often spilled into violence in Pakistan, and there has been a wave of such incidents in recent months in Punjab and North West Frontier province, in which scores of people were killed.
Sunnis dominate Pakistan's population of about 130 million, of which Shi'ites constitute about 15 percent.
